units.title: Actual PBPS: why the reflected augmented transition preserves its target

sources.label: Proposition3.4, equation3.11 and Algorithm2; standing1.1/scale2.2; reflectionProp2.1iii and conditional reversibilityProp3.2
sources.scope: Exact one-step invariance of the literal augmented transition only. No process restart/semigroup, augmented all-L2 operator, hypocoercivity or quantitative convergence, implementation error/caps/cost, warm-start initialization, composition or complete paper.

assumptions: The six standing analytic binders are unchanged: genuine C2/Hessian bounds, positive alpha and eta, alpha<=beta and beta eta<=1. The only new source binders are the fixed scalar rho and 0<rho<1; weights do not depend on state.

The potential, Gaussian, canonical volume and Hilbert-space assumptions match the actual half-turn producer. fderiv is totalized in Lean, but C2 supplies genuine differentiability; no derivative-zero fallback is used to infer regularity.

Gibbs integrability/positive normalizer, probability, explicit everywhere-defined q_y, joint measurable kernels, conditional disintegration, mixture mass one and invariant measures are internally derived, not supplied premises.

Conditional R is the explicit normalized quadratic tilt at EVERY y. Its equality to the retained R follows from their explicit fiber laws, not from almost-everywhere uniqueness of arbitrary conditional versions.
All old path coverage/initialization null sets remain parameterwise. This one-step law does not assert a temporal Markov/restart/semigroup property or any convergence rate.
units.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including dimension zero. Suppose \(V\in C^2\), \(0<\alpha\le\beta\), \(\alpha\|v\|^2\le D^2V(x)[v,v]\le\beta\|v\|^2\) for all \(x,v\), \(\eta>0\), \(\beta\eta\le1\), and a fixed scalar \(0<\rho<1\). Let \(\mu(dx)\propto e^{-V(x)}dx\) and let \(J\) be the law of \((X,X+\sqrt\eta G)\) for independent \(X\sim\mu\), \(G\sim\mathcal N(0,I)\). Let \(q_y(dx)\propto e^{-V(x)-\|x-y\|^2/(2\eta)}dx\) and let \(H_y(x,\cdot)\) be the actual time-pi returned-position kernel, with an independent reference from \(q_y\), Gaussian momentum and iid unit exponential clocks. Reflect \(y\) to \(y\prime=2x-y\), draw the next position from \(\rho q_{y\prime}+(1-\rho)H_{y\prime}(x,\cdot)\), and retain \(y\prime\). This defines a Markov kernel \(K\) preserving \(J\). All probability normalizations and the conditional-kernel certificate are conclusions. The same literal clock recursion, covered-arc/fallback laws, parameterwise AE coverage/initialization, and actual H witness are retained in the folded full statement.

steps.title: Normalize the real target and identify the SAME conditional kernel
steps.text: The genuine Hessian lower bound gives a finite positive Gibbs normalizer. The existing Gaussian augmentation is therefore a probability law. Its explicit backward conditional is a quadratic exponential tilt of mu. The nested-tilt identity turns it into the literal volume tilt q_y. Both conditional kernels have this fiber at every y, so they are equal as kernels; we transfer the disintegration certificate to the R retained by the actual half-turn producer.
steps.detail: This is pointwise identity of explicitly chosen versions, not a pointwise claim obtained from AE conditional uniqueness. Integrability is established before applying the normalized nested-tilt identity.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨Z, hZM, hZa, hZf, hgood, R, hR, hRq, H, hHK, hrev, hHlaw, hH0, hHgood⟩ :=
    ActualHalfTurnReversibility.actual_half_turn_reversible hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  letI : IsMarkovKernel R := hR
  letI : IsMarkovKernel H := hHK
  have hnorm := GibbsAugmentation.normalized_augmentation_density
    hα hV (fun x v => (hH x v).1) hη
  have hi : Integrable (fun x : E => Real.exp (-V x)) (volume : Measure E) :=
    Integrable.of_integral_ne_zero hnorm.1.ne'
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := isProbabilityMeasure_tilted hi
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure J := hnorm.2.1
  obtain ⟨Rc, hRc, hRctilt, hcond⟩ :=
    TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianConditionalKernel.exists_tilted_isCondKernel μ hη
  have hRcq (y : E) : Rc y = q y := by
    rw [hRctilt y, show μ = (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x) from rfl,
      tilted_tilted hi]
    congr 1
    funext x
    dsimp only [Pi.add_apply]
    ring
  have hRcR : Rc = R := by
    ext y : 1
    rw [hRcq y, hRq y]
  subst Rc
  change (J.map Prod.swap).IsCondKernel R at hcond
  letI : (J.map Prod.swap).IsCondKernel R := hcond

steps.title: Mix two probability updates at fixed auxiliary coordinate
steps.text: The actual half-turn is reversible for q_y, hence invariant. Exact resampling has the constant output law q_y and also preserves it. Construct their jointly measurable fixed two-component mixture F using the existing finite-mixture API. The nonnegative weights sum to one, so F is Markov; its restriction to each y preserves q_y.
steps.formula: \begin{aligned}q_y H_y&=q_y,\quad q_y R_y=q_y,\\ F_y(x)&=\rho q_y+(1-\rho)H_y(x),\qquad q_y F_y=q_y.\end{aligned}
steps.detail: The excerpt implements the mixture adapter: its private hH input is discharged from actual reversibility in the public proof. It is not a new public hypothesis. State-dependent selection weights would invalidate this inference.
steps.lean:
private theorem reflected_conditional_mixture
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (J : Measure (E × E)) [IsProbabilityMeasure J]
    (R : Kernel E E) [IsMarkovKernel R] [(J.map Prod.swap).IsCondKernel R]
    (H : Kernel (E × E) E) [IsMarkovKernel H]
    (hH : ∀ y, (H.comap (fun x => (y, x)) (by fun_prop)).Invariant (R y))
    (ρ : ℝ) (hρpos : 0 < ρ) (hρlt : ρ < 1)
    (hreflection : J.map (fun z => (z.1, (2 : ℝ) • z.1 - z.2)) = J) :
    ∃ K : Kernel (E × E) (E × E), IsMarkovKernel K ∧ K.Invariant J ∧
      ∀ z, K z = (ENNReal.ofReal ρ • R ((2 : ℝ) • z.1 - z.2) +
        ENNReal.ofReal (1 - ρ) • H ((2 : ℝ) • z.1 - z.2, z.1)).prod
        (Measure.dirac ((2 : ℝ) • z.1 - z.2)) := by
  classical
  let w : Fin 2 → ℝ≥0 := ![Real.toNNReal ρ, Real.toNNReal (1 - ρ)]
  have hw : ∑ i, w i = 1 := by
    apply NNReal.coe_injective
    simp only [Fin.sum_univ_two, w, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one,
      NNReal.coe_add, NNReal.coe_one, Real.coe_toNNReal ρ hρpos.le,
      Real.coe_toNNReal (1 - ρ) (sub_nonneg.mpr hρlt.le)]
    ring
  let A : Kernel (E × E) E := R.comap Prod.fst measurable_fst
  let ks : Fin 2 → Kernel (E × E) E := ![A, H]
  letI : ∀ i, IsMarkovKernel (ks i) := by
    intro i
    fin_cases i <;> dsimp [ks, A] <;> infer_instance
  let F := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelMixture.finiteMixture w ks
  letI : IsMarkovKernel F :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelMixture.finiteMixture_isMarkovKernel w ks hw
  have hFlaw (z : E × E) : F z = ENNReal.ofReal ρ • R z.1 +
      ENNReal.ofReal (1 - ρ) • H z := by
    rw [AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelMixture.finiteMixture_apply,
      Fin.sum_univ_two]
    rfl
  have hF (y : E) : (F.comap (fun x => (y, x)) (by fun_prop)).Invariant (R y) := by
    let sy : Fin 2 → Kernel E E :=
      ![Kernel.const E (R y), H.comap (fun x => (y, x)) (by fun_prop)]
    letI : ∀ i, IsMarkovKernel (sy i) := by
      intro i
      fin_cases i <;> dsimp [sy] <;> infer_instance
    have hsy : ∀ i, (sy i).Invariant (R y) := by
      intro i
      fin_cases i
      · change (R y).bind (fun _ => R y) = R y
        simp [Measure.bind_const]
      · exact hH y
    have heq : F.comap (fun x => (y, x)) (by fun_prop) =
        AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelMixture.finiteMixture w sy := by
      ext x : 1
      rw [Kernel.comap_apply, hFlaw,
        AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelMixture.finiteMixture_apply,
        Fin.sum_univ_two]
      rfl
    rw [heq]
    exact AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelMixture.finiteMixture_invariant
      w sy (R y) hw hsy

steps.title: Explain the omitted retained-coordinate Tonelli argument
steps.text: Work in the order (y,x), with nu=J.swap. For any measurable set S, write S_y for its measurable section. The lifted update L keeps y and draws xprime from F_y(x). Disintegrate nu; Tonelli applies to these nonnegative measurable probabilities. Fiber invariance replaces the inner integral by q_y(S_y), and the same disintegration recovers nu(S). Thus L preserves the entire joint law, not only its marginals.
steps.formula: \begin{aligned}(\nu L)(S)&=\int J^Y(dy)\int q_y(dx)F_y(x,S_y)\\&=\int J^Y(dy)q_y(S_y)=\nu(S),\\ S_y&=\{x:(y,x)\in S\}.\end{aligned}
steps.detail: No unbounded signed integral, moment assumption or extra domination premise is needed. Kernel measurability and section measurability are explicit; the implementation uses ENNReal lintegrals and the exact conditional certificate.
steps.lean:
private theorem retained_invariant {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B]
    (ν : Measure (A × B)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (R : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel R] [ν.IsCondKernel R]
    (F : Kernel (A × B) B) [IsMarkovKernel F]
    (hF : ∀ a, (F.comap (fun b => (a, b)) (by fun_prop)).Invariant (R a)) :
    ((Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst) ×ₖ F).Invariant ν := by
  let L := (Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst) ×ₖ F
  change ν.bind L = ν
  ext s hs
  calc
    (ν.bind L) s = ∫⁻ z, L z s ∂ν :=
      Measure.bind_apply hs L.aemeasurable
    _ = ∫⁻ a, ∫⁻ b, L (a, b) s ∂R a ∂ν.fst := by
      rw [← Measure.lintegral_compProd (L.measurable_coe hs), ν.disintegrate R]
    _ = ∫⁻ a, R a (Prod.mk a ⁻¹' s) ∂ν.fst := by
      apply lintegral_congr
      intro a
      simp_rw [show ∀ b, L (a, b) s = F (a, b) (Prod.mk a ⁻¹' s) from
        fun b => Kernel.deterministic_prod_apply' measurable_fst F (a, b) hs]
      have ht : MeasurableSet (Prod.mk a ⁻¹' s) := hs.preimage measurable_prodMk_left
      have hi := congrArg (fun m : Measure B => m (Prod.mk a ⁻¹' s)) (hF a).def
      rw [Measure.bind_apply ht (Kernel.aemeasurable _)] at hi
      exact hi
    _ = (ν.fst ⊗ₘ R) s := (Measure.compProd_apply hs).symm
    _ = ν s := congrArg (fun m : Measure (A × B) => m s) (ν.disintegrate R)

steps.title: Swap coordinates back, then apply reflection first
steps.text: Conjugating L by the measurable swap returns to the order (x,y), giving an invariant Markov kernel B. The existing Gaussian reflection U(x,y)=(x,2x-y) preserves J. Define K as first U, then B. Composition of two J-preserving kernels preserves J. Evaluating the kernel removes the deterministic input and swaps the product factors, giving exactly the displayed transition law.
steps.detail: The order matters: the conditional mixture is evaluated at the reflected auxiliary coordinate, not the original y. Kernel.map can totalize to zero for nonmeasurable maps; here genuine swap/reflection measurability is proved, and Markovness is checked separately.
steps.lean:
letI : IsProbabilityMeasure (J.map Prod.swap) :=
    Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map measurable_swap.aemeasurable
  let L : Kernel (E × E) (E × E) :=
    (Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst) ×ₖ F
  have hL : L.Invariant (J.map Prod.swap) := retained_invariant (J.map Prod.swap) R F hF
  let B : Kernel (E × E) (E × E) := (L.comap Prod.swap measurable_swap).map Prod.swap
  letI : IsMarkovKernel B := Kernel.IsMarkovKernel.map _ measurable_swap
  have hB : B.Invariant J := by
    have ht := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelTransport.invariant_map_comap
      (MeasurableEquiv.prodComm : E × E ≃ᵐ E × E) hL
    change B.Invariant ((J.map Prod.swap).map Prod.swap) at ht
    rw [Measure.map_map measurable_swap measurable_swap] at ht
    simpa only [Prod.swap_swap_eq, Measure.map_id] using ht
  let U : E × E → E × E := fun z => (z.1, (2 : ℝ) • z.1 - z.2)
  have hU : Measurable U := by
    dsimp only [U]
    fun_prop
  have hUinv : (Kernel.deterministic U hU).Invariant J := by
    change (Kernel.deterministic U hU) ∘ₘ J = J
    rw [Measure.deterministic_comp_eq_map]
    exact hreflection
  let K := B ∘ₖ Kernel.deterministic U hU
  refine ⟨K, inferInstance, hB.comp hUinv, ?_⟩
  intro z
  change (B ∘ₖ Kernel.deterministic U hU) z = _
  rw [Kernel.comp_deterministic_eq_comap, Kernel.comap_apply, Kernel.map_apply _ measurable_swap,
    Kernel.comap_apply, Kernel.prod_apply, Kernel.deterministic_apply]
  rw [Measure.prod_swap, hFlaw]
  rfl

steps.title: Connect every adapter to the actual process, with no supplied invariant law
steps.text: The public proof retains the actual jointly measurable Z and its exact H pushforward, covered-arc/fallback equations and local initialization. It derives the fiber invariant input from the retained every-y detailed balance, obtains reflection from the owned Gaussian producer, and invokes the private construction. Finally replace the exact R fibers by q_y to obtain the paper transition, without replacing H by an arbitrary convenient kernel.
steps.detail: Local compilation proves this proposition. Independent source review, integration and purification are separately tracked. In particular, invariant law alone supplies none of the later hypocoercivity or actual expected-cost conclusions.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance, Z, hZM, hZa, hZf, hgood, R, hR, hRq,
    H, hHK, hrev, hHlaw, hH0, hHgood, hcond, ?_⟩
  have hHinv (y : E) : (H.comap (fun x => (y, x)) (by fun_prop)).Invariant (R y) := by
    rw [hRq y]
    exact (hrev y).invariant
  have href : J.map (fun z => (z.1, (2 : ℝ) • z.1 - z.2)) = J :=
    (GaussianReflection.reflection_preserves_augmentation μ η hη).2
  obtain ⟨K, hK, hKinv, hKlaw⟩ :=
    reflected_conditional_mixture J R H hHinv ρ hρpos hρlt href
  refine ⟨K, hK, hKinv, ?_⟩
  intro z
  simpa only [hRq] using hKlaw z

units.lean_proof: Normalize and identify explicit conditional -> fixed conditional mixture -> measurable-section Tonelli lift -> swap transport -> reflection-first composition -> same actual K law.
